uncited: Unlike traditional 3DGS which requires dense pose estimation and iterative optimization [6136-instantsplat.md], these methods either predict primitives and poses directly via a feed-forward network [6137-anysplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md] or initialize Gaussians using geometry priors from foundation models to enable rapid, pose-free training [6136-instantsplat.md].

They solve the problem of local minima and computational cost inherent in sparse-view reconstruction by enabling real-time inference and eliminating the dependency on incremental depth priors or temporal continuity [6464-pixelsplat.md, 6888-joint-pose-optimization.md].

Loss functions typically combine photometric reconstruction error, such as $\mathcal{L}_{L1}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{MSE}$, with perceptual or structural metrics like $\mathcal{L}_{MS-SSIM}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{LPIPS}$ [6136-instantsplat.md][6464-pixelsplat.md].
Each conv layer preceded by normalization and Swish activation.
The family originates from the need to generalize 3D Gaussian Splatting beyond single-scene optimization, which is computationally expensive and requires accurate initial poses [6464-pixelsplat.md].

Early work like pixelSplat [6464-pixelsplat.md] introduced feed-forward architectures to predict Gaussian primitives directly from image pairs, addressing the local minima issues of traditional splatting.
Joint Pose Optimization [6888-joint-pose-optimization.md] provides an alternative by treating poses as learnable parameters rather than predicting them via a network.
These methods are used in generalizable novel view synthesis, 3D object reconstruction from sparse views, and applications requiring real-time rendering from casual captures [6464-pixelsplat.md, S1].
